mainTopic: Whether a debt creates a lien (שיעבוד) by Torah law, and the source that a husband's death frees his wife to remarry
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier point: the word 'פרצו' in הושע, written without 'and', shows that each sin brings punishment on its own. Next comes a משנה: if a woman brought her חטאת after childbirth and died, her heirs bring her עולה. שמואל says this applies only if she set the animal aside while alive, so a lien (שיעבוד) is not from the Torah. רבי יוחנן says the heirs bring it even if she never set it aside, so a lien is from the Torah. The גמרא asks why they argue again, since they already disagreed about a loan made without a document (מלוה על פה). It answers that both cases are needed, and רב פפא rules that such a loan is collected from heirs but not from buyers. The גמרא then asks how we know a husband's death frees his wife to remarry. Logic, the יבמה, and the widow forbidden to a כהן גדול are each tried and pushed aside, and so is the פסוק 'another man take her'. רב אשי settles it: a יבם is never called 'another', and the Torah links death to divorce, so death frees her completely. The amud ends by asking for the source that a יבמה is acquired through ביאה, and the פסוק is quoted on the next amud.

steps.title: Each sin is punished separately
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves from the wording of the פסוק that the punishment applies to each sin on its own, not only when all the sins are done together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does the פסוק say 'and they break out'? No, it says 'they break out.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a question from just before this section: maybe the punishment in the פסוק only comes when someone does all the listed sins together. It answers by pointing to the exact wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק had said 'ופרצו' (with 'and'), all the sins would read as one package. Since it says 'פרצו' without 'and', it starts a new idea that applies to each sin by itself. So even the sin of misusing גיטין and קידושין is enough for the punishment alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it written...? A way of pointing to the exact wording of a פסוק
They broke out / broke all bounds (הושע 4:2)
AND they broke out. This wording is not in the פסוק.

steps.whatToRemember: One small letter (the 'ו', meaning 'and') can change how a פסוק reads: without it, each sin carries the punishment on its own.

phrases.english: Is it written 'and they break out'?
'They break out' is written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from just before this section: whether the punishment requires all the sins together.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the פסוק's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The punishment only comes when all the listed sins are done together.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the פסוק says 'פרצו' without 'and', each sin carries the punishment on its own.

steps.title: The משנה about a woman who died before bringing her עולה
steps.stepSummary: The Sages sat again and discussed a משנה: if a woman brought her חטאת after childbirth and then died, her heirs bring her עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sat again and said: about what we learned in a משנה, that if a woman brought her חטאת and then died, the heirs bring her עולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a משנה. This step sets up the next move, where אמוראים argue about exactly when the heirs must bring the עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After childbirth a woman owes two קרבנות: a חטאת and an עולה. Here she brought only the חטאת before she died. The משנה rules that her heirs still bring the עולה, which raises a question: are the heirs paying off her 'debt' to הקדש from her property?

keyTerms.meaning: They sat again and said: opens another discussion
That we learned (in a משנה)
Sin-offering
Burnt-offering
Heirs

phrases.english: They again sat and said:
That which we learned in a משנה:
A woman who brought her sin-offering and died
phrases.notes: This is a woman after childbirth, who owes both a חטאת and an עולה.

phrases.english: the heirs bring her burnt-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion, unrelated to the פסוק in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a woman brought her חטאת and died, her heirs bring her עולה.

steps.title: שמואל limits the משנה; a lien is not from the Torah
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the heirs bring the עולה only if she already set aside the animal while alive. The גמרא concludes that he holds a lien (שיעבוד) is not from the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: this applies only if she set the animal aside while she was alive. If she did not, the heirs do not bring it. So it seems שמואל holds that a lien is not from the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל narrows the משנה to a case where the animal was already set aside. The גמרא then explains what this tells us about his view of debts and liens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If her obligation created a Torah lien on all her property, the heirs would have to bring the עולה from the estate either way. Since שמואל requires that she already set aside the animal, a general obligation alone does not tie up her property. That means שיעבוד is not דאורייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: She set it aside / designated it (for the קרבן)
While alive
Apparently / this shows that
He holds
A lien: a debt that ties up the debtor's property
From the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: Here the 'debt' is a debt to Heaven (a קרבן she owes), not a debt to a person. The גמרא treats it with the same lien logic as an ordinary loan.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
And that is when she set it aside in her lifetime.
But if she did not set it aside in her lifetime, no.
Apparently he holds
a lien is not from the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: וְהוּא שֶׁהִפְרִישַׁתָּה מֵחַיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the משנה from step 2 and draws a principle from that limit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Heirs bring the עולה only if she set it aside while alive. This shows שמואל holds שיעבוד is not דאורייתא.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן disagrees; a lien is from the Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the heirs bring the עולה even if she never set it aside. This shows he holds that a lien (שיעבוד) is from the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: even if she did not set it aside while alive. So it seems he holds that a lien is from the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the opposite ruling to שמואל's. The גמרא draws the opposite principle from his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, her obligation to bring an עולה already tied up her property, like a debt. So the heirs must pay it from the estate even without a set-aside animal. That means שיעבוד is דאורייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Even though
Is (counts as)

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל: the animal must be set aside, so a lien is not from the Torah. רבי יוחנן: no setting aside is needed, so a lien is from the Torah.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב שֶׁלֹּא הִפְרִישַׁתָּה מֵחַיִּים.
phrases.english: Even though she did not set it aside in her lifetime.
Apparently he holds:
a lien is from the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אַף עַל גַּב שֶׁלֹּא הִפְרִישַׁתָּה מֵחַיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to שמואל's in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Heirs bring the עולה even if it was not set aside. This shows רבי יוחנן holds שיעבוד is דאורייתא.

steps.title: They already argued about this: רב and שמואל on a loan without a document
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why they argue here, since they already argued about liens. רב and שמואל hold that a loan made without a document cannot be collected from heirs or from buyers.
steps.simpleTranslation: But they already argued about this once! רב and שמואל both said: a loan made without a document cannot be collected from the heirs or from the buyers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the need for the argument in steps 3–4. The same question, whether a lien is from the Torah, was already argued about regarding loans made without a document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A loan made without a document (מלוה על פה) has no written lien. If רב and שמואל let the lender collect from heirs or buyers, that could only be because the Torah itself creates a lien. They say he cannot collect, so they hold שיעבוד is not דאורייתא, the same position as שמואל above. Why repeat the argument?

keyTerms.meaning: But they already argued about it
One time (already)
A loan made orally, without a document
Collects (payment)
Buyers (who bought land from the borrower)
Both of them

phrases.english: But they already disagreed about it once,
as Rav and Shmuel both say:
A loan by mouth (without a document)
is not collected from the heirs
nor from the buyers.
phrases.notes: These are people who bought land from the borrower after he took the loan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the argument between שמואל and רבי יוחנן in steps 3–4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for a second argument about the עולה case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same אמוראים already argued about whether שיעבוד is דאורייתא in the case of מלוה על פה, so arguing again seems repetitive.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש: a loan without a document can be collected
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes its proof: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש hold that a loan without a document can be collected from heirs and from buyers.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש both said: a loan made without a document is collected both from the heirs and from the buyers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the other side of the earlier argument. This shows that רבי יוחנן already took the position that a lien is from the Torah. The next step answers the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Collecting a loan without a document from heirs and buyers only works if the Torah itself puts a lien on the borrower's property. So רבי יוחנן's view here matches his ruling about the עולה. That makes the challenge stronger: the same argument appears twice.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, רבי יוחנן's main partner in learning
Both... and...

steps.whatToRemember: The challenge: רב and שמואל (a lien is not from the Torah) and רבי יוחנן with ריש לקיש (a lien is from the Torah) already argued about loans without a document. So why argue again about the עולה?

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish both say:
A loan by mouth
is collected both from the heirs
and from the buyers.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the evidence for the challenge begun in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן already held שיעבוד is דאורייתא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש that מלוה על פה is collected from heirs and buyers

steps.title: Both disputes are needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the argument had to be stated in both the loan case and the עולה case, because each case has a special reason that could have changed one side's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both are needed. If we only heard the loan case, we might think שמואל says there is no lien only there, because a private loan is not written in the Torah. In the עולה case, we might think he agrees with רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש. And if we only heard the עולה case, we might think רבי יוחנן says there is a lien only there, because a debt written in the Torah is like one written in a document. In a private loan, we might think he agrees with שמואל. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question from Step 5: why did they need to argue twice? It says each case teaches something the other case could not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A private loan is weaker, because the Torah does not write it down. The woman's עולה is stronger, because the Torah itself commands it. So we might have guessed that שמואל gives in on the strong case, or that רבי יוחנן gives in on the weak case. Stating both disputes shows that each one holds his view in both cases.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary: both statements are needed, and neither is extra
A debt written in the Torah, meaning an obligation the Torah itself creates
It is like a debt written in a document
Agrees, gives in to the other opinion

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the words 'this' and 'that' (בהא / בהך) carefully. They switch back and forth between the private loan and the woman's עולה. Keep track of which case each one points to.

phrases.english: It is necessary, for if it were stated only about this case,

phrases.english: because it is a loan not written in the Torah,
but in that other case, I would say

phrases.english: he agrees with רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.
And if they had taught us only in this case,

because a debt written in the Torah

phrases.english: but in that case, the private loan, I would say he agrees with שמואל,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Steps 5–6 about why the dispute is repeated.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each case has its own reason, so both are needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each disputant might give in on the case that is more favorable to the other side.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל denies a Torah lien even for a Torah-created debt, and רבי יוחנן holds a Torah lien even for a private loan.

steps.title: The final ruling on oral loans
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that a creditor of an oral loan can collect from the borrower's heirs but not from people who bought his land.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The law is that with an oral loan, the lender collects from the heirs but not from the buyers. He collects from the heirs because the lien is from the Torah. He does not collect from the buyers because an oral loan is not publicly known.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the practical final law on loans made without a document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He follows the view that a lien is from the Torah, so the heirs must pay. He adds a new reason to protect buyers: an oral loan has no publicity, so the buyers had no way to know about it. It is unfair to take land away from them.

keyTerms.meaning: The law is (the final practical ruling)
An oral loan, made without a written document
A lien on property that comes from the Torah
Buyers who purchased land from the borrower
Publicity, meaning people have heard about the loan

steps.whatToRemember: Final law: an oral loan is collected from heirs, because a שיעבוד is from the Torah. It is not collected from buyers, because nobody knew about the loan.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical הלכה for oral loans. It balances two ideas: the Torah lien and fairness to buyers who did not know about the debt.

phrases.english: רב פפא said: The law is,

phrases.aramaic: מִלְוָה עַל פֶּה – גּוֹבֶה מִן הַיּוֹרְשִׁין,
phrases.english: with an oral loan, he collects from the heirs,
but he does not collect from the buyers.
He collects from the heirs because the lien is from the Torah,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ גּוֹבֶה מִן הַלָּקוֹחוֹת – דְּלֵית לֵיהּ קָלָא.
phrases.english: and he does not collect from the buyers because it has no publicity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both disputes are shown to be needed, the גמרא gives the practical ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: An oral loan is collected from heirs, because the שיעבוד is from the Torah, but not from buyers, because it has no publicity.

steps.title: A divorce document has a clear source in the Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's rule that a woman goes free through a גט or her husband's death. It says a גט clearly has a פסוק, which sets up a question about the husband's death.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: And she acquires herself through a divorce document and through the husband's death. It makes sense for a divorce document, because it is written: 'And he writes her a scroll of severance.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic from the משנה. This step is a setup: it agrees that a גט has a clear source, and is preparing to ask where the Torah says a husband's death frees her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בשלמא ('it makes sense') is a signal. It tells us the גמרא accepts one part and is about to ask about the other part. The פסוק about the גט is clear, but no פסוק has yet been shown for the husband's death.

keyTerms.meaning: She acquires herself, meaning she becomes free from the marriage
The husband's death
It makes sense for this part, which introduces a question about another part
A scroll of severance, the Torah's name for a גט

phrases.english: And she acquires herself
through a divorce document and through the husband's death.
It makes sense for a divorce document, as it is written:
"And he writes her a scroll of severance."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section, going back to the next clause of the משנה after the lien discussion ends.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source in the Torah for the rule that the husband's death frees the wife. This part of the question comes next.

steps.title: What is the source that the husband's death frees her?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that מיתת הבעל frees a woman to remarry.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the husband's death, from where do we learn it?
steps.whatsHappening: We already have a פסוק for a גט. Now the גמרא asks for the source of the second way the משנה gave: the husband's death. This question sets up the search that fills the rest of this section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said a woman goes free in two ways. Step 9 showed that a גט has a clear פסוק. Now the גמרא wants an equally solid source for מיתת הבעל.

keyTerms.meaning: the husband's death
from where do we know it?

phrases.english: But the death of the husband, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the setup from step 9 by asking the actual question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a husband's death permits his wife to marry others.

steps.title: Logic: the one who forbade her is gone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a סברא: the husband made her forbidden, and his death takes the prohibition away.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is logic: he made her forbidden, and he makes her permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says no פסוק is needed. Plain logic tells us that the husband's death frees her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibition on a married woman exists only because of the husband. Once he is no longer alive, nothing is left to keep her forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: logical reasoning (as opposed to a פסוק)
he made her forbidden
he makes her permitted

phrases.english: It is logical reasoning:
he forbade her, and he permits her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is logic: the husband caused the prohibition, so his death removes it.

steps.title: Challenge from relatives who stay forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the סברא from עריות: the husband makes her forbidden to his relatives, and his death does not permit her to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about the forbidden relatives? He makes her forbidden to them, and he does not permit her to them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the logic of step 11. It points to a case where the husband caused a prohibition that does not go away when he dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Marriage makes a woman forbidden to the husband's relatives, such as his father or his son. Those prohibitions stay even after he dies. So the idea that "what he forbade, his death permits" cannot be a general rule.

keyTerms.meaning: forbidden relationships, here the husband's relatives
"but look at", which opens a challenge

phrases.english: But what about the forbidden relatives,
phrases.notes: For example, a son may not marry his father's wife even after his father dies.

phrases.english: whom he forbids her to, and does not permit her to!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the סברא given in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The סברא: הוא אסרה והוא שרתה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The husband's marriage creates prohibitions with his relatives that his death does not remove, so the logic does not work.

steps.title: New source: the childless widow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the סברא and learns from יבמה: a childless widow is forbidden to others, so a widow with children must be permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, since the Torah says a יבמה who has no children is forbidden, it follows that if she has children she is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on logic and turns to a פסוק. It reads the law of יבום "from the opposite side" to learn about every widow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah forbids a childless widow to marry outside the family because she waits for the יבם. That implies a widow with children has no such limit, so her husband's death must have freed her.

keyTerms.meaning: since the Torah (literally, the Merciful One) said
a childless widow who waits for her husband's brother
children

phrases.english: Rather, since the Merciful One said
a יבמה who has no children is forbidden,
it follows that if she has children, she is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected סברא with a source from a פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule comes from the law of יבמה, read in reverse.

steps.title: Maybe a widow with children is forbidden to everyone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: maybe the childless widow is allowed only to the יבם, and a widow with children is forbidden to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps: without children she is forbidden to the world but permitted to the יבם, and with children she is forbidden to everyone too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the proof from יבמה does not hold. The same פסוק could be read in a way that does not free the widow at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference between the two widows might be only about the יבם. A childless widow has one man she may marry, and a widow with children has no one. With that reading, nothing is learned about her being free to marry others.

keyTerms.meaning: but perhaps, which offers another reading
the dead husband's brother
to the world, meaning to everyone else

phrases.english: But perhaps:
if she has no children, she is forbidden to everyone
and permitted to the יבם,
and if she has children,
she is forbidden to everyone as well!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִילְמָא אֵין לָהּ בָּנִים אֲסוּרָה לְעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof given in step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from יבמה as a source for מיתת הבעל.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The inference could be only about the יבם and not about permitting her to others.

steps.title: New source: the widow and the כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא learns from the rule that an אלמנה is forbidden to a כהן גדול. That implies she is permitted to a כהן הדיוט.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, since the Torah says a widow is forbidden to a כהן גדול, it follows she is permitted to an ordinary כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third source. Singling out the כהן גדול shows that other men may marry a widow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a widow were forbidden to everyone, the Torah would have no reason to forbid her specially to a כהן גדול. So she must be permitted to an ordinary כהן, and to a regular Jew all the more.

keyTerms.meaning: a widow
the High Priest
an ordinary כהן

phrases.english: Rather, since the Merciful One said
a widow is forbidden to a כהן גדול,
it follows that to an ordinary כהן she is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִדְּאָמַר רַחֲמָנָא אַלְמָנָה לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof from יבמה with a new one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule came from the law of יבמה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule comes from the prohibition of a widow to a כהן גדול.

steps.title: Maybe she is still forbidden to everyone, just more lightly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the כהן גדול has a לאו, while everyone else is still forbidden to her by a lighter עשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps to a כהן גדול she is forbidden by a negative commandment, and to everyone else by a positive commandment?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to weaken the new proof. Maybe the כהן גדול is singled out only because his prohibition is stronger, not because others are allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading, the widow would be forbidden to everyone. The only difference would be how serious the prohibition is: a לאו for the כהן גדול and an עשה for others.

keyTerms.meaning: a negative commandment ("do not")
a positive commandment, which is lighter here

phrases.english: But perhaps to a כהן גדול she is forbidden by a לאו,
and to everyone else by an עשה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to reject the proof given in step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from אלמנה לכהן גדול.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Singling out the כהן גדול might show only a stronger prohibition, not that others are permitted.

steps.title: No middle ground: either fully free or still married
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea of an עשה. Either the husband's death worked and she is fully free, or it did not and she is still a married woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: What would this עשה be for? If the husband's death has an effect, she should be fully permitted. If it has no effect, she should stay in her first status!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the כהן גדול proof against the challenge of step 16 by arguing that a light עשה makes no sense here. The next step pushes back on this argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A light עשה prohibition makes no sense here. If the death ended the marriage, nothing is left to forbid her. If it did not, she is still a married woman with the full prohibition. Since the Torah shows she is permitted to a כהן הדיוט, the death must free her completely.

keyTerms.meaning: what is its job? what would it be doing?
had an effect
let her be fully permitted
the earlier status

steps.whatToRemember: The claim here is that there is no in-between status: either she is still a married woman or she is fully free. Step 18 challenges this, and the final source comes in Step 21.
steps.whyThisMatters: This all-or-nothing argument is what Step 18 challenges. The point that death fully ends the marriage is finally proven by רב אשי's הקש in Step 21.

phrases.english: This עשה, what would it be doing?
If the husband's death had an effect,
let her be fully permitted,
and if the husband's death had no effect,
let her stay in her first status!
phrases.notes: Her first status means a married woman, where being with another man carries the death penalty, not just an עשה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge of step 16, so the proof of step 15 stands.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the suggested in-between status is impossible
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe a widow stays forbidden to everyone by a light עשה.
steps.terutzMaskana: For now, the claim is that there is no middle status, so the כהן גדול proof would stand. Step 18 challenges this with the case of redeemed פסולי המוקדשים.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For now, the argument is that a husband's death must either free her fully or not at all. Step 18 rejects this.

steps.title: Maybe death only lowers her prohibition, like blemished sacrificial animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the claim from Step 17. Maybe the husband's death moved her from a death-penalty prohibition down to a lighter עשה, just as redeemed פסולי המוקדשים lose מעילה but stay forbidden for shearing and work.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why not? Maybe his death took her out of the death-penalty prohibition and put her under a positive commandment. That is just like consecrated animals that became disqualified. At first, the rules of misusing holy property apply to them, and it is forbidden to shear them or work with them. Once they are redeemed, misuse no longer applies, but shearing and working with them are still forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the idea from Step 17 that there are only two choices: fully free or still married. It shows a case where a change removes one prohibition but leaves a lighter one in place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 said a middle state makes no sense. This step answers that the הלכה does have middle states: a blemished קרבן that is redeemed loses מעילה but keeps the ban on shearing and work. So maybe a widow likewise loses the death-penalty level of אשת איש but stays forbidden by an עשה, and the earlier proof falls.

keyTerms.meaning: Why not? This opens a challenge to the claim just made
Animals set aside as קרבנות that became unfit, usually through a blemish
Misusing holy property for personal benefit
Shearing the animal's wool and making it do work
He redeemed them, exchanging their holiness for money

steps.confusionAlert: The comparison is not saying a widow is holy property. It only shows that one event can remove a heavy prohibition while a lighter one stays.

phrases.english: And why not?
It took her out of death
phrases.notes: 'It' is the husband's death, and 'death' is the death penalty for being with a married woman.

phrases.english: and placed her under a positive commandment,
just as it is with disqualified consecrated animals,
that at first are subject to misuse of holy property,
and are forbidden for shearing and work.
Once he redeemed them, misuse does not apply to them,
yet they are still forbidden for shearing and work.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְּמָה לָא? אַפִּיקְתַּהּ מִמִּיתָה וְאוֹקֵימְתַּהּ עַל עֲשֵׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects Step 17's claim that a middle state of prohibition cannot exist.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The logical argument of Step 17 that she must be either fully free or fully married, and with it the proof from אלמנה לכהן גדול in Step 15.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There is a known parallel in redeemed פסולי המוקדשים, where a heavy prohibition goes away and a lighter one stays.

steps.title: A new source: 'Lest he die in battle and another man take her'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the indirect inferences and brings a פסוק showing that after a soldier dies, another man may marry his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we learn it from what the verse says: 'Lest he die in battle and another man take her.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on the indirect inferences from other laws and brings a direct פסוק. The verse speaks of a soldier's widow being married by 'another man.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier proofs were each pushed aside: the יבמה proof because she might be forbidden to everyone, and the כהן גדול proof because a lighter prohibition might remain. This פסוק openly describes another man marrying the widow, so it seems to show she is permitted to remarry.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It marks dropping the previous approach for a new one
A verse
Another man

phrases.english: Rather, from what the verse says:
"Lest he die in battle
and another man take her."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 18 knocks out the logical proof, the גמרא switches to a verse.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the widow stays forbidden by an עשה, like redeemed פסולי המוקדשים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק describes another man marrying the widow, so she is permitted.

steps.title: Maybe 'another man' means only the יבם
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי objects that the 'other man' in the פסוק could be the יבם, so the verse does not prove she may marry anyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי objected: Say that the 'other man' is the יבם!
steps.whatsHappening: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי attacks the new proof. He suggests the verse may only allow the dead man's brother, the יבם, to marry her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This brings back the doubt from Step 14: maybe the widow may only be taken through יבום. If 'another man' means the יבם, the פסוק says nothing about marrying a stranger.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenges it, raising a strong objection
Say, or perhaps. It offers another way to read the source
The brother of a man who died childless, who may marry the widow

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rav Sheisha, son of Rav Idi, objected to this:
Say: who is the 'other'? The yavam!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of the verse brought in Step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from 'another man take her.'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The words 'another man' could refer only to the יבם.

steps.title: רב אשי: two answers prove death fully frees her
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives two answers. A יבם is never called 'another.' Also, the תורה links death to divorce, so death fully frees her just as a גט does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: There are two answers to this. First, a יבם is not called 'another.' Also, it is written: 'And the latter husband hates her and writes her a document of severance' and 'or if the latter husband dies.' The פסוק puts death side by side with divorce. Just as divorce permits her and fully ends the marriage, so too death permits her and fully ends the marriage.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי defends the proof against רב שישא's objection with two separate answers. The second answer also settles the whole question of whether any prohibition remains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First answer: a יבם continues the first husband's marriage, so the תורה would not call him 'another.' Second answer: the פסוק places death next to divorce, and a גט frees a woman to marry anyone with nothing left over. Death must therefore do the same, which also ends the worry from Step 18 that a leftover עשה might remain.

keyTerms.meaning: There are two answers to this matter
A document of severance, a גט
It was compared or linked, by placing two things side by side in a פסוק (a הקש)
Permits her and completes the ending of the marriage

steps.whatToRemember: A husband's death frees his wife completely, just like a גט. She may marry anyone, not only the יבם, and no lighter prohibition remains.
steps.whyThisMatters: The הקש between death and divorce answers both open doubts in this סוגיא: whether only a יבם may marry her, and whether a leftover עשה remains.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
There are two answers to this matter:
One, that a yavam is not called 'another.'
And also: it is written:
"And the latter man hates her
and writes her a document of severance"
"or if the latter man dies,"
so death is compared to divorce:
just as divorce permits her and completes the separation,
so too death permits her and completes the separation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: שְׁתֵּי תְּשׁוּבוֹת בַּדָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב שישא's objection in Step 20 and confirms the proof from Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two answers: the meaning of the word 'another,' and a הקש of death to divorce
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Another man' might mean only the יבם, and some lighter prohibition might remain.
steps.terutzMaskana: A יבם is never called 'another,' and death, like divorce, fully frees her to marry anyone.

steps.title: Quoting the next line of the משנה about the יבמה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה: a יבמה is acquired through ביאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: a יבמה is acquired through ביאה, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the topic of a married woman going free and moves on by quoting the next line of the משנה. This sets up a question about that line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יבמה is a widow whose husband died with no children, and his brother (the יבם) must marry her or do חליצה. The משנה teaches that the יבם makes her his wife only through ביאה, not through money or a document like a regular קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow whose husband died childless, who is bound to his brother
The dead husband's brother, who may marry the widow
Intercourse
Is acquired (becomes his wife)

phrases.english: And a yevama is acquired through intercourse, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the discussion of a married woman going free (Steps 9-21) to the next clause of the משנה about the יבמה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A יבמה becomes the wife of the יבם only through ביאה.

steps.title: Asking for the source that intercourse acquires a יבמה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that ביאה acquires a יבמה, and starts its answer: 'the פסוק says.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do we learn that she is acquired through ביאה? The פסוק says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source in the תורה that ביאה is what makes the יבמה the wife of the יבם. It then begins its answer with 'the פסוק says', getting ready to quote a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a request for a source, not an attack on the משנה. The גמרא wants to see where the תורה shows that ביאה, specifically, is how ייבום is done. The words 'אמר קרא' are a setup: the actual פסוק comes right after.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?
The פסוק says (introduces a source from the תורה)

phrases.english: Through intercourse — from where do we derive this?
The verse states:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule just quoted from the משנה in Step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source in the תורה showing that ביאה is how a יבם acquires a יבמה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer begins with 'אמר קרא': a פסוק will be brought (quoted next).
